data.title: Clotrimazole + Beclomethasone cream
data.summary: V Steroid combinations · Combination: imidazole antifungal (clotrimazole 1%) + potent fluorinated steroid (beclomethasone dipropionate 0.025%)
data.body:
_Topicals · V Steroid combinations_

**Class:** Combination: imidazole antifungal (clotrimazole 1%) + potent fluorinated steroid (beclomethasone dipropionate 0.025%)

## Mechanism of action
- Clotrimazole: ergosterol synthesis inhibitor
- Beclomethasone: rapid relief of itch and inflammation

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Limited valid use: short-term (under 1–2 weeks) for highly inflamed candidal intertrigo or dermatophyte infection, under a doctor's supervision
- In practice it is heavily misused (OTC) in India for any itchy rash

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily for a maximum of about 1–2 weeks; then continue plain antifungal

## Adverse effects
- Steroid-modified tinea (tinea incognito) — extensive, atypical, chronic, recurrent dermatophytosis
- Atrophy, striae (especially groin and thighs), telangiectasia, topical steroid dependence
- Majocchi granuloma (deep fungal folliculitis), treatment failure, increasing antifungal resistance

## Contraindications
- Tinea when used for more than a short period; children, face, flexures (steroid absorption)
- Not for self-medication

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Irrational/misused FDC — a key driver of India's chronic dermatophytosis epidemic
- Many steroid–antifungal–antibiotic FDCs were banned by the Indian government in 2018; IADVL campaigns against steroid misuse
- Treat tinea with antifungal alone

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.42 and ch.45 (misuse of combinations); Khopkar ch.19 and ch.22; IADVL taskforce on steroid abuse. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
